correctness.rationale: For a (2,1,1) allocation every comparison to another singleton is automatic after removal. A singleton agent facing the pair must value her own good at least as much as the lesser of the two paired goods. Thus actual EF1 depends only on strict orders when no ties occur, and any allocation surviving a strict tie refinement also satisfies the original weak inequalities. Relabeling the goods to fix the first order is unique and preserves the labeled allocation count; the other five orders run independently over all 24 possibilities. An independent exact program built the 36 candidate allocations by surjective assignments, used literal cardinal EF1 on utilities 4,3,2,1 in the respective orders, and accumulated the histogram by profile chunks. All 7,962,624 profiles and every reported cell matched, with minimum two, maximum eighteen, minimum proportion 1/1152, and first moment 64/9. The latter also follows by counting the four independent singleton-agent tests of probability 2/3 for each allocation. Direct cardinal checks gave exactly the two displayed balanced allocations for the sharpness witness, and zero among the 243 complete allocations of the prior five-good example. With at most three goods each occupied group can have a singleton. This proves four-good universal multiplicity and the smallest complete EF1 nonexistence size of five.
residual_risks: Histogram and upper bound eighteen are for strict ranks; ties and zeros are included only in the universal lower-bound assertion.
Nonnegativity, additivity, fixed pairs and labeled complete allocations are essential to the checked reduction.

value.rationale: Four goods is the last open size immediately before the known five-good failure and the first size for which singleton-only allocation cannot solve EF1. The sharp positive multiplicity shows unavoidable choice among balanced labels even in the tight case, and the full strict census quantifies how often that case and all other multiplicities occur. This is a natural small-instance frontier, useful as an exact benchmark, not an arbitrarily sized enumeration.
residual_risks: This does not imply efficient allocation for variable item counts or a probability law for valuations containing ties.
